title: IELTS General
content_provenance: Original practice items authored from the public IELTS General Training syllabus. Not a capture of past exam questions.

items.stem: A community notice states that the new library will open on Mondays to Fridays from nine in the morning until six in the evening and will stay closed at weekends. When does the new library open?
options: On weekdays from nine until six
items.explanation: The notice gives opening on Mondays to Fridays, which are weekdays, from nine until six, and states the library is closed at weekends.

items.stem: A workplace memo says that all new staff must complete fire-safety training within their first two weeks and then refresher training every year after that. How often must staff repeat the refresher training?
items.explanation: The memo sets the initial training within two weeks and then states refresher training every year, so annual repetition is required.

items.stem: A letter tells an applicant that the offer is provisional and will be confirmed only once satisfactory references are received. In the letter, the word provisional most nearly means what?
items.explanation: The offer is provisional until references arrive, so provisional means temporary and not yet final rather than permanent or withdrawn.

items.stem: A job advertisement asks for someone who can work unsupervised and is willing to travel to client sites around the region. What does the advertisement suggest about the role?
options: It needs no experience at all
items.explanation: Asking for unsupervised work and travel to client sites points to a role needing independence and travel, not a fixed office job.

items.stem: A bus timetable shows that the 7.15 service from Mill Road reaches the station at 7.50 and that later services all leave thirty minutes after the previous one. What time does the stated 7.15 service reach the station?
items.explanation: The timetable states plainly that the 7.15 service arrives at 7.50, so the other times are not supported by the text.

items.stem: A short article argues that learning a second language improves memory and concentration as well as communication, so schools should teach languages from an early age. What is the article's main argument?
options: Languages should be taught only to adults
Language learning has wider benefits and should start early
Language learning wastes valuable school time
Memory and concentration cannot be trained
items.explanation: The article lists memory, concentration and communication benefits and urges early teaching, so it argues for wider benefits and an early start.

items.stem: A report warns that the repairs will be substantial and could take several months to finish because the roof must be replaced. In the report, the word substantial most nearly means what?
items.explanation: Repairs taking months and involving a new roof indicate a large extent, so substantial means large rather than minor or quick.

items.stem: A gym leaflet states that members may bring one guest per visit and that guests must sign in at reception before using any equipment. What must a guest do before using the equipment?
items.explanation: The leaflet requires guests to sign in at reception first, and nothing about a joining fee or a class appears in the text.

items.stem: A park notice explains that paths may flood after heavy rain and advises walkers to check the daily forecast before setting out. What does the notice advise walkers to do?
items.explanation: The notice links flooding to heavy rain and advises checking the forecast, so walkers are told to check before setting out.

items.stem: A college prospectus says the evening computing course runs for ten weeks and costs twenty pounds, which includes all materials. What does the stated fee include?
items.explanation: The prospectus says the twenty-pound fee includes all materials, so no laptop or single class is offered by the text.

items.stem: An article claims that higher parking charges may deter drivers from entering the town centre during the busiest hours. In the article, the word deter most nearly means what?
items.explanation: Charges intended to keep drivers away mean deter, which is to discourage someone from doing something.

items.stem: A recorded message says the clinic is closed for staff training on the first Wednesday of each month and that patients should call back the following day. When is the clinic closed for training?
options: The first Wednesday of each month
items.explanation: The message names the first Wednesday of each month as the closure time, so the other options are not given.

items.stem: A staff handbook explains that employees should report accidents immediately, however minor, so that hazards can be fixed before anyone is hurt again. Why should accidents be reported at once?
options: So hazards can be fixed before further harm
So blame can be assigned quickly
So the building can be closed
items.explanation: The handbook gives the reason that hazards can be fixed before anyone is hurt again, not to assign blame or close the building.

items.stem: A rental advert describes a flat with two bedrooms, a shared garden and off-street parking, and states that the rent is due on the first of each month. When is the rent due?
options: On the first of each month
On the last day of the year
items.explanation: The advert states the rent falls due on the first of each month, so the weekly and yearly options are unsupported.

items.stem: The article says the council was reluctant to approve the plan until residents raised concerns about traffic, after which it agreed. In the article, reluctant most nearly means what?
items.explanation: The council only agreed after concerns were raised, so reluctant means unwilling or hesitant rather than eager.

items.stem: A sign at the entrance states that the trail is unsuitable for wheelchairs because of steep steps and loose gravel along the route. What does the sign suggest about the trail?
options: It is fully accessible to everyone
It is closed to all visitors
It is reserved for cyclists only
It is difficult for wheelchair users
items.explanation: Calling the trail unsuitable for wheelchairs because of steps and gravel suggests it is difficult for wheelchair users.

items.stem: A leaflet explains that to register a new address you must bring proof of identity, a recent utility bill and a completed form to the local office. Which of these is required?
items.explanation: The leaflet lists a utility bill among the required documents, while the photograph, certificate and bank statement are not mentioned.

items.stem: The passage explains that repairing household appliances instead of replacing them saves money and reduces the amount of waste sent to landfill. What is the passage's main point about repairs?
options: Repairs save money and reduce waste
Replacement is always the better choice
Waste levels are not a concern
items.explanation: The passage presents repairs as saving money and cutting landfill waste, so the main point combines both benefits.

items.stem: A travel article notes that the region is remote and its bus services are sparse, running only twice a week. In the article, sparse most nearly means what?
items.explanation: Services running only twice a week show that sparse means thinly spread or infrequent rather than frequent.

items.stem: A festival programme states that the concert begins at eight in the evening and that doors open an hour earlier for ticket holders. When do the doors open for ticket holders?
items.explanation: An hour before the eight o'clock concert is seven in the evening, which is when the doors open for ticket holders.

items.stem: In a station announcement the speaker says the train to York will depart from platform six instead of platform four. Which platform will the train to York depart from?
items.explanation: The announcement changes the departure to platform six, explicitly replacing the earlier platform four.

items.stem: A caller books a table for four people at seven thirty on Saturday and gives the name Okafor for the reservation. How many people is the table booked for?
items.explanation: The caller requests a table for four people, so seven and thirty are numbers from the time rather than the party size.

items.stem: In a campus tour the guide says the sports centre stands behind the main library and right next to the swimming pool. What is next to the sports centre?
items.explanation: The guide places the sports centre next to the swimming pool, while the station, car park and town hall are not mentioned.

items.stem: A customer tells a shop assistant that a kettle stopped working after two days and asks for a replacement rather than a repair. What does the customer want?
items.explanation: The customer asks for a replacement rather than a repair, so a replacement kettle is the requested outcome.

items.stem: In a museum talk the speaker says the oldest exhibit is a stone tool dated to about twelve thousand years ago and that it was found locally. What does the speaker say about the stone tool?
items.explanation: The speaker describes the stone tool as the oldest exhibit, dated to about twelve thousand years ago and found locally.

items.stem: A receptionist tells a caller the dentist can see them on Tuesday at half past nine and asks them to arrive ten minutes early to complete some forms. When should the caller arrive?
items.explanation: Ten minutes before half past nine is twenty past nine, which is when the caller is asked to arrive.

items.stem: In a travel report the presenter says heavy rain is expected in the north of the country but the south should stay dry and sunny all week. What weather is expected in the south?
items.explanation: The presenter contrasts rain in the north with dry and sunny conditions in the south all week.

items.stem: A lab demonstrator tells students to put on safety glasses before switching on the burner and to keep them on until the experiment ends. When may students remove the safety glasses?
options: In the middle of the experiment
As soon as they enter the room
items.explanation: The demonstrator says to keep the glasses on until the experiment ends, so they may be removed only afterwards.

items.stem: One speaker suggests meeting at the cafe, and the other replies that the library would be much quieter for studying together. Where does the second speaker prefer to meet?
items.explanation: The second speaker suggests the library as quieter for studying, so that is the preferred meeting place over the cafe.

items.stem: A gym instructor says the new class has twenty places and that twelve of them have already been taken by members. How many places remain in the class?
items.explanation: Subtracting the twelve taken places from twenty total places leaves eight places still available.

items.stem: A student explains that an essay was handed in late because the library's printer jammed and the technician took an hour to fix it. Why was the essay late?
options: The library was closed that day
items.explanation: The student blames a jammed printer and the repair time, so a printer fault caused the delay.

items.stem: An airport announcement says the flight to Dublin is delayed by ninety minutes because of thick fog over the runway. Why is the flight delayed?
items.explanation: The announcement attributes the ninety-minute delay to thick fog over the runway, not to a strike or fault.

items.stem: A radio advert says the furniture sale is at the warehouse on Bridge Road, directly opposite the old cinema and beside the river. Where is the warehouse located?
options: On Bridge Road opposite the old cinema
items.explanation: The advert places the warehouse on Bridge Road opposite the old cinema, so the other locations are unsupported.

items.stem: A caller says that the room was not what they expected, though the staff were very kind and helpful. What is the caller's overall attitude?
options: Disappointed with the room but positive about the staff
items.explanation: The caller was let down by the room yet praises the staff, giving a disappointed but partly positive attitude.

items.stem: A guide says the walking tour covers five kilometres and lasts about three hours, including a short break at a cafe. How long does the tour last?
items.explanation: The guide gives the duration as about three hours, while five refers to kilometres and is not a time.

items.stem: A driving instructor tells the learner to check the mirrors, signal, and then move off only when the road is clear. What should the learner do immediately before moving off?
options: Check that the road is clear
items.explanation: The instructor makes moving off conditional on the road being clear, so checking that is the final step before moving.

items.stem: A manager says the team meeting will move from Wednesday to Thursday because most members are attending a course on Wednesday. Why is the meeting moved?
options: Most members are on a course Wednesday
The meeting room is too small
The manager is away all week
items.explanation: The manager gives the Wednesday course attended by most members as the reason for moving the meeting to Thursday.

items.stem: A voicemail says the parcel will be delivered between two and four in the afternoon and that a signature is required on receipt. What is required when the parcel arrives?
items.explanation: The voicemail states a signature is required on receipt, and no payment or passport is mentioned.

items.stem: A customer says the meal was excellent and that they would happily recommend the restaurant to all their friends. How does the customer feel about the restaurant?
options: Very positive and willing to recommend it
items.explanation: Calling the meal excellent and offering to recommend the restaurant shows a very positive view of it.

items.stem: An organiser tells volunteers the stall opens at ten and that they should arrive half an hour before that to help set everything up. When should volunteers arrive?
items.explanation: Half an hour before the ten o'clock opening is half past nine, which is when volunteers should arrive.

items.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence. If it rains tomorrow, we ___ cancel the picnic in the park.
items.explanation: In the first conditional, an if-clause in the present simple is matched with will plus the base verb in the main clause.
items.reference: IELTS General Training Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence. She is very good ___ solving difficult problems under pressure.
items.explanation: The adjective good is followed by the preposition at when describing a skill, as in good at solving problems.
items.reference: IELTS General Training Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence. The company has grown quickly and now needs more ___ staff at every level.
items.explanation: An adjective is needed before the noun staff, and experienced is that adjective, while experience and experiences are nouns.
items.reference: IELTS General Training Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence. This is the ___ interesting book I have ever read.
items.explanation: The superlative most is used with a longer adjective before the phrase I have ever read, comparing three or more items.
items.reference: IELTS General Training Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence. You ___ take an umbrella because it looks like rain later.
items.explanation: Should expresses sensible advice, whereas must not and cannot express prohibition or impossibility and do not fit this advice.
items.reference: IELTS General Training Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence. He studied hard for weeks, ___ he still found the exam difficult.
items.explanation: Although introduces the contrast between studying hard and still finding the exam difficult, which is the intended meaning.
items.reference: IELTS General Training Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence. Please ___ the form and hand it to the receptionist today.
items.explanation: Fill in means to complete a form, while look after means to care for and put off means to postpone, which do not fit.
items.reference: IELTS General Training Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence. The list of applicants ___ grown longer with every passing week.
items.explanation: The subject is the singular noun list, not applicants, so the singular verb has agrees with it in the present perfect.
items.reference: IELTS General Training Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Which option is closest in meaning to the word ample as it is used in the sentence There was ample time to finish the test?
items.explanation: Ample means more than enough or plentiful, so it does not mean exactly enough, very little or none at all.
items.reference: IELTS General Training Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence. The manager asked the whole team to ___ a decision before Friday.
items.explanation: Make collocates with decision in English, while do, bring and hold do not form the standard phrase make a decision.
items.reference: IELTS General Training Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence. The meeting is scheduled ___ Monday morning in the main hall.
items.explanation: On is used with days and dates, so on Monday morning is correct, while in is used with months and at with clock times.
items.reference: IELTS General Training Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence. She said that she ___ finished the report the day before.
items.explanation: In reported speech the past perfect had finished reports a past event that occurred before the moment of speaking.
items.reference: IELTS General Training Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence. He is ___ honest man who always keeps his word to others.
items.explanation: An is used before a vowel sound, and honest begins with a silent h and therefore a vowel sound, so an is correct.
items.reference: IELTS General Training Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence. She speaks English ___ than her younger brother does.
items.explanation: The comparative more fluently is used with than, whereas fluent is an adjective and most fluently is a superlative.
items.reference: IELTS General Training Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Which option is closest in meaning to the word brief as it is used in the phrase a brief meeting with the director?
items.explanation: Brief means short in duration, so a brief meeting is a short one rather than a long, cancelled or merely formal one.
items.reference: IELTS General Training Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence. She enjoys ___ books in the evening after work.
items.explanation: The verb enjoy is followed by a gerund, so reading is correct, not the infinitive to read or the bare forms.
items.reference: IELTS General Training Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence. The woman ___ car was stolen called the police straight away.
items.explanation: Whose shows possession before the noun car, whereas who and whom refer to people and which refers to things.
items.reference: IELTS General Training Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence. The train arrived ___ time despite the heavy snow overnight.
items.explanation: On time is the fixed phrase meaning punctually, while in time means before a deadline and at time is not standard.
items.reference: IELTS General Training Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Which option is closest in meaning to the word cautious as it is used in the sentence She was cautious about lending money?
items.explanation: Cautious means careful to avoid risk or danger, so it is the opposite of reckless rather than a synonym for generous.
items.reference: IELTS General Training Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary

items.stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence. Her ___ of the problem impressed the whole team greatly.
items.explanation: A noun is needed after the possessive her, and understanding acts as a noun here, while understand is a verb.
items.reference: IELTS General Training Syllabus - Grammar and Vocabulary
